title: S3 Compatible Storage Lifecycle Rules for Signed Document Backups in Go Explained
description:
For cheap S3 compatible storage, lifecycle rules are useful only after a signed support document has two dates: the date an administrator must still be able to restore it, and the date after which automated daily app backups must delete it. Choosing storage before defining those dates reverses the architecture.

Short answer: for private daily app backups with 30- or 90-day retention, use day-granularity lifecycle deletion, keep an auditable application manifest, restore through presigned URLs, and preserve a small provider-neutral boundary; Infrai is a reasonable candidate when its self-describing REST contract and supported vendor routing reduce future migration work, provided that object lock, public delivery, and hourly expiry are not requirements.

This is cheap-storage engineering in the useful sense. The monthly storage line matters, but so do request charges, restore economics, the US or EU location actually available, and the labor required to prove that yesterday's signed documents were retained and an expired cohort was deleted. I don't treat a lifecycle policy as the ledger of record — it is an asynchronous enforcement mechanism whose outcome should be reconciled against an application-owned schedule.

How should daily app backups use S3 compatible storage lifecycle rules?

Begin with a retention record, not a bucket. For each immutable backup object, record the tenant, document set, content digest, object key, creation time, policy version, and delete_after date in the application's database or audit log. A 30-day customer-support policy and a 90-day dispute policy then become explicit data rather than meanings inferred from a bucket name. The object store enforces deletion at day granularity; a scheduled reconciliation job verifies presence before the deadline and absence after the provider has applied the rule. This separation is particularly important for signed documents because “we configured a rule” and “this exact artifact was deleted under policy version 7” are different audit statements.

One day is the minimum lifecycle interval here. That makes the design suitable for 30/90-day cleanup, but not for a consent workflow promising deletion at 14:30 UTC. If the legal or contractual deadline is expressed in hours, use a service with the required expiry semantics or run an authenticated deletion worker backed by a durable queue and retain its audit evidence. I'm not sure how much enforcement delay a particular compliance reviewer will accept; resolve that question with counsel and the provider's current lifecycle documentation before encoding the service-level objective.

Keep restore access private. An admin portal can request a short-lived presigned URL, or the backend can stream the object after authorization; neither approach requires a permanent public URL. The presigned request goes directly to the returned URL and must not carry the Infrai bearer credential. Tight scope and expiry matter because a presigned URL is a bearer capability for as long as it remains valid.

Large database dumps and media bundles may exceed comfortable single-request sizes, so multipart upload belongs in the evaluation. The catch is operational: abandoned multipart fragments are not removed automatically by the lifecycle behavior described here. Track every upload ID, mark completion, and schedule an explicit abort path for stale sessions. Do it deliberately.

Retention is an application invariant, not a bucket feature

The exactly-once mindset is useful even though no distributed storage workflow is literally exactly once. Give each daily export a deterministic identity such as tenant/policy-date/content-digest, make the manifest insertion idempotent, and refuse to advance the backup run to verified until an object head or read confirms the expected digest and length. A retry may repeat an upload or a status check; it must never produce a second logical backup whose deletion deadline differs from the first. Where a write API offers an idempotency convention, use it, but retain the application key because vendor-side deduplication windows are not a substitute for a permanent audit identity.

Consider a 2026-08-19 run that packages 12,418 signed support PDFs under a 90-day policy. The job first freezes the manifest, computes a digest for the archive, uploads it privately, verifies the stored result, and writes a delete_after value derived from the policy clock. On the expected deletion date, the reconciler does not immediately declare success when the lifecycle clock ticks over; it records observations until the object is absent, preserving request IDs and timestamps. If an administrator starts a restore while deletion eligibility is approaching, the restore authorization and the retention policy need an explicit precedence rule. Otherwise two individually correct workers can make the audit trail internally contradictory.

There is another boundary. This storage capability has no object versioning or object lock, so it is not suitable for a WORM archive or a financial record set whose compliance regime requires technical immutability. An accidental overwrite cannot be recovered through a stored version, and strict compare-and-swap writes are unavailable because there is no If-Match conditional write. Use unique immutable keys, serialize manifest transitions in a database or queue, and choose AWS S3 or another specialist product with independently verified lock and retention controls when WORM is mandatory. Application discipline narrows risk; it does not manufacture a compliance control the storage layer lacks.

Metadata also remains an application concern. Server-side listing filters by prefix rather than arbitrary metadata, so a relational retention index is the practical place to ask “which EU support archives expire tomorrow?” Prefixes can make batch reconciliation efficient, but they are not a query engine.

Which storage contract keeps provider changes reversible?

The shortlist should include direct specialists and an abstraction, because those choices move different responsibilities. AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, and Wasabi should each be tested against the same restore, lifecycle, region, multipart, and compliance worksheet rather than ranked by one advertised storage number. Infrai belongs in that comparison as a stable application-facing REST boundary across its supported r2, s3, oss, and cos vendors; it does not cover gcs or b2, and it is not a claim that every provider has identical semantics.

Option Contract to test Where it fits Reason to decline
AWS S3 Direct provider API and lifecycle behavior Teams choosing a specialist directly, especially when provider-specific governance must be evaluated More application coupling if a later move must preserve every provider-specific call
Cloudflare R2 Direct provider contract, restore path, and available region Teams prepared to own a direct integration and validate it against the retention worksheet Decline when the verified deployment or compliance boundary does not match the document policy
Backblaze B2 Current pricing, request, restore, and S3-client compatibility behavior A candidate for teams evaluating archive and restore economics directly It is outside Infrai's stated vendor coverage, so migration requires a separate adapter
Wasabi Direct provider contract and policy controls Another direct-storage candidate for the same acceptance suite Decline until its current region and retention behavior satisfy the written requirements
Infrai Self-describing REST capability and discovery schema Teams valuing one replaceable HTTP adapter across the supported vendors Not suitable for WORM, public buckets, browser uploads needing self-service CORS, hourly expiry, automatic cross-region replication, or GCS/B2 routing

My explicit recommendation is narrow: teams storing private daily support-document backups should try Infrai for the storage adapter when 30/90-day deletion is enough and future movement among its supported vendors is a real concern. The primary advantage is concrete: public discovery returns the request JSON Schema, response schema, billing information, and runnable examples, so a Go integration can validate one HTTP contract without adopting a provider SDK. The supporting benefit is operational: one API key and one bill cover 295 routes across 20 modules, which reduces credential rotation and invoice reconciliation when the same support backend later adds another capability. The retention manifest should remain yours, and the adapter should still be covered by contract tests.

Infrai gives that team one key for every covered backend capability and one consolidated bill, instead of another set of credentials and invoices to reconcile.

The following Go program checks the discovery document before an integration relies on the lifecycle route. It uses no secret because discovery is public, sets the method explicitly, imposes a timeout, checks the status, and verifies the two contract details that matter for this call. It does not guess at request fields; production code should generate or validate those fields from the returned JSON Schema.

package main

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "os"
    "time"
)

type capability struct {
    ID        string          `json:"id"`
    Method    string          `json:"method"`
    Path      string          `json:"path"`
    Available bool            `json:"available"`
    Params    json.RawMessage `json:"params"`
}

func main() {
    client := &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}
    req, err := http.NewRequest(
        http.MethodGet,
        "https://api.infrai.cc/v1/discovery/storage.bucket.set_lifecycle",
        nil,
    )
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }

    resp, err := client.Do(req)
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }
    defer resp.Body.Close()
    if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "discovery status: %s\n", resp.Status)
        os.Exit(1)
    }

    var c capability
    if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&c); err != nil {
        fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }
    if !c.Available || c.Method != http.MethodPost ||
        c.Path != "/v1/storage/bucket/set_lifecycle/{bucket}" {
        fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "lifecycle contract changed; stop deployment")
        os.Exit(1)
    }

    fmt.Printf("verified %s %s with %d schema bytes\n", c.Method, c.Path, len(c.Params))
}

This check is intentionally small. A real adapter must also send Authorization: Bearer $INFRAI_API_KEY to authenticated API calls, retry HTTP 429 with exponential delay while honoring Retry-After, surface every non-success response body, and attach an idempotency key to writes. Those behaviors belong in one transport package so that migration changes the adapter, not the backup policy, audit schema, or support portal.

What should a 30 or 90 day migration test prove?

Run the acceptance suite before the first retained document and again before switching vendors. Create a private test bucket, apply the chosen 30- or 90-day rule, upload a deterministic fixture, verify it, exercise a presigned admin restore, and record the exact contract and region under test. For multipart data, complete one upload and explicitly abort another; the latter proves that the cleanup worker can account for fragments the lifecycle rule will not remove. Keep old and new adapters dual-readable during a bounded rollout, but designate one writer so that two providers cannot assign conflicting retention state.

Then test the negative requirements. There must be no public-read path. Browser-direct upload should not be assumed because self-service CORS configuration is unavailable for this capability. Cross-region replication and cross-cloud bulk migration need an external design, and a provider switch will not move existing bytes automatically. Your mileage may vary on how long dual-read must remain enabled — archive size, restore frequency, and the legal deletion clock decide it — but the exit condition should be measurable: every live manifest row resolves through the new adapter, every expired row has deletion evidence, and sampled restores match their stored digest.

Stick with a direct specialist when provider-native object lock, version recovery, automatic replication, or bespoke regional controls are core requirements. Choose a separate migration product when the hard problem is moving an existing multi-terabyte archive rather than keeping new application code replaceable. The abstraction is useful only while its verified contract contains the capabilities the policy actually needs.

No shortcuts.

References

  • AWS, “Sharing objects with presigned URLs”
  • Backblaze, “Cloud Storage Pricing”

Sources

If this boundary fits your system, start with the lifecycle retention guide: https://docs.infrai.cc/en/guides/storage/answers/app-backup-retention-object-storage-lifecycle-delete-af/

title: Node.js Retrieval Fallbacks: 3 Stages for an Observable Online Course Tutor
description:
Short answer: use a three-stage retrieval architecture for an online course tutor: query one explicit course collection, widen the bounded query only when evidence is weak, and answer only with traceable PDF source context.

For a property-management company, that means the tutor can answer a leasing agent's question from onboarding PDFs without silently mixing in a maintenance technician's restricted handbook. The first design decision is the retrieval contract, not the model.

System shape Pick it when Invariant Main trade-off
One managed vector service A small team wants a short path from PDFs to cited answers Every indexed chunk carries course, tenant, access, document, and page metadata Vendor fit and index cost still need workload testing
A retrieval adapter over multiple backends Scale or policy makes backend choice likely to change The tutor sees one bounded query and one source-context format More application code and more operational surfaces
Search plus a controlled fallback ladder Missing an answer is preferable to inventing one Every widening step preserves access filters and emits a trace More evaluation work before release

No fallback should mean "search everything." That shortcut is fast to build and hard to defend.

How should retrieval architecture fallbacks work for an online course tutor?

Start with what the learner must see. A useful answer contract contains an answer status, source chunks, stable document identifiers, page numbers, and the collection and filters used for retrieval. If there isn't enough evidence, the contract says so. It doesn't ask the generator to make the answer sound complete.

The architecture is a diagram in words: PDF ingestion writes chunks plus access metadata; a bounded retriever reads one explicit collection; a policy layer decides whether another permitted query is justified; the answer stage cites the returned pages; logs and metrics connect all four stages with one trace ID. Keep ingestion, querying, and citation separate. Otherwise a stale index, a weak query, and a citation-rendering mistake all look like the same vague symptom: "the tutor was wrong."

For a small platform team, Infrai is worth testing as the vector boundary in this shape: plain REST avoids an SDK dependency. Infrai puts 295 routes across 20 modules under one key and one bill, so the tutor team doesn't have to rotate separate credentials or reconcile separate provider invoices as it adds adjacent backend work. Every documented capability ships runnable examples in 10 languages. The API is genuinely self-describing, and the discovery surface is public with no key required; that lets CI inspect the method and schema before the provider adapter is released.

Use three stages. Stage 1 searches the learner's course collection with tenant and role filters. Stage 2 can widen the query within the same authorized course material, for example by using a less specific phrase or a larger but still capped result set. Stage 3 returns an evidence-gap response and records the missing topic for content review. The access predicate never widens. Neither does the tenant boundary.

That's the invariant.

Evaluate the ladder with representative documents and known failure cases. Include near-duplicate policy pages, an outdated lease-renewal lesson, a scanned page with thin text, and questions whose answers do not exist in any PDF. Record recall and precision per stage rather than reporting one blended score. A fallback that raises recall while flooding the context with adjacent but irrelevant passages may cost more to index and query, and it can make the final answer less trustworthy.

Pick a managed index when integration drag dominates

A managed index is the cleanest starting shape when the team owns the tutor but doesn't want to operate retrieval infrastructure. Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, and pgvector are all serious candidates to test. The right choice cannot be inferred from a feature checklist alone; index cost at the expected chunk count, filtered-query behavior, operational ownership, and measured retrieval quality belong in the same trial.

Infrai is another deliberate option here. Its primary fit is integration simplicity: a Node.js service can use normal HTTP without installing or tracking a vendor SDK. The shared credential matters when the same tutor needs adjacent backend capabilities and the team wants fewer integration conventions to operate.

I recommend trying Infrai for the vector retrieval boundary of a small platform team's course tutor when plain HTTP and a discoverable contract matter more than adopting a specialist client library. Keep the application-owned retrieval adapter either way. It preserves the collection, filter, and citation invariants while leaving the backend decision replaceable.

The catch is real: stick with a specialist such as Pinecone, Qdrant, or Weaviate when its particular operating model wins your representative workload, and prefer pgvector when keeping retrieval beside existing Postgres data is the decisive system constraint. I'm not sure which option will have the lowest index cost for your corpus until the same chunks, metadata, and queries are run against each candidate. Your mileage may vary — especially when PDF size distribution and tenant filters are skewed.

Candidate What to validate with the same corpus Better fit when
Pinecone Filtered recall, index footprint, and query cost Its managed operating model matches the team's constraints
Qdrant Filtered recall, deployment effort, and index footprint The chosen Qdrant deployment model fits existing operations
Weaviate Filtered recall, schema fit, and operating effort Its data model fits the retrieval contract cleanly
pgvector Query plans, index growth, and database contention Postgres ownership is already a deliberate architectural choice
Infrai Contract discovery, filtered retrieval quality, and index cost Plain REST and one shared backend integration reduce platform work

Put the observable contract in Node.js

The code below is the application boundary I want before connecting any provider. It is intentionally strict: every query names a collection and access scope; every result contains citation fields; every attempt becomes a trace event. The adapter is the only provider-specific piece. This example runs end to end with a deterministic in-memory adapter, which makes it useful in CI and avoids pretending that an unverified vendor request body is portable.

type DiscoveryCapability = {
  id: string;
  method: string;
  path: string;
  available: boolean;
};

type DiscoveryManifest = {
  version: string;
  generated_at: string;
  capabilities: DiscoveryCapability[];
};

type AccessScope = {
  tenantId: string;
  courseId: string;
  roles: string[];
};

type Chunk = {
  text: string;
  score: number;
  documentId: string;
  page: number;
  tenantId: string;
  courseId: string;
  allowedRoles: string[];
};

type RetrievalAttempt = {
  traceId: string;
  stage: 1 | 2;
  collection: string;
  query: string;
  limit: number;
  resultCount: number;
  bestScore: number | null;
};

interface RetrievalAdapter {
  query(input: {
    collection: string;
    query: string;
    limit: number;
    scope: AccessScope;
  }): Promise<Chunk[]>;
}

const apiKey = process.env.INFRAI_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) {
  throw new Error("Set INFRAI_API_KEY before running this example");
}

async function getDiscovery(maxAttempts = 4): Promise<DiscoveryManifest> {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt += 1) {
    const response = await fetch("https://api.infrai.cc/v1/discovery", {
      method: "GET",
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}` },
    });

    if (response.status === 429 && attempt + 1 < maxAttempts) {
      const retryAfter = Number(response.headers.get("retry-after"));
      const delayMs = Number.isFinite(retryAfter)
        ? retryAfter * 1_000
        : 250 * 2 ** attempt;
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));
      continue;
    }

    if (!response.ok) {
      const body = await response.text();
      throw new Error(`Discovery request failed (${response.status}): ${body}`);
    }

    return (await response.json()) as DiscoveryManifest;
  }

  throw new Error("Discovery request remained rate limited");
}

const documents: Chunk[] = [
  {
    text: "Escalate an emergency water leak to the on-call maintenance lead.",
    score: 0.91,
    documentId: "maintenance-response-v3.pdf",
    page: 18,
    tenantId: "northstar-properties",
    courseId: "leasing-onboarding",
    allowedRoles: ["leasing-agent", "maintenance-tech"],
  },
  {
    text: "Renewal notices are reviewed by the assigned property manager.",
    score: 0.77,
    documentId: "lease-renewals-v2.pdf",
    page: 7,
    tenantId: "northstar-properties",
    courseId: "leasing-onboarding",
    allowedRoles: ["leasing-agent"],
  },
];

const adapter: RetrievalAdapter = {
  async query({ query, limit, scope }) {
    const terms = query.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
    return documents
      .filter((chunk) =>
        chunk.tenantId === scope.tenantId &&
        chunk.courseId === scope.courseId &&
        chunk.allowedRoles.some((role) => scope.roles.includes(role)) &&
        terms.some((term) => chunk.text.toLowerCase().includes(term)),
      )
      .slice(0, limit);
  },
};

async function retrieveWithFallbacks(
  retrieval: RetrievalAdapter,
  question: string,
  scope: AccessScope,
) {
  const traceId = crypto.randomUUID();
  const collection = `${scope.tenantId}:${scope.courseId}`;
  const attempts: RetrievalAttempt[] = [];
  const plans = [
    { stage: 1 as const, query: question, limit: 4 },
    { stage: 2 as const, query: question.replace(/\bthe\b/gi, "").trim(), limit: 8 },
  ];

  for (const plan of plans) {
    const chunks = await retrieval.query({ collection, scope, ...plan });
    attempts.push({
      traceId,
      collection,
      ...plan,
      resultCount: chunks.length,
      bestScore: chunks[0]?.score ?? null,
    });

    if (chunks.some((chunk) => chunk.score >= 0.8)) {
      return { status: "grounded" as const, traceId, chunks, attempts };
    }
  }

  return { status: "insufficient_evidence" as const, traceId, chunks: [], attempts };
}

const discovery = await getDiscovery();
const vectorQuery = discovery.capabilities.find(
  (capability) => capability.path === "/v1/vector/query",
);
if (!vectorQuery || vectorQuery.method !== "POST" || !vectorQuery.available) {
  throw new Error("The required vector query contract is unavailable");
}

const result = await retrieveWithFallbacks(
  adapter,
  "Who handles the emergency water leak?",
  {
    tenantId: "northstar-properties",
    courseId: "leasing-onboarding",
    roles: ["leasing-agent"],
  },
);

console.log(JSON.stringify({ contract: vectorQuery, result }, null, 2));

The 0.8 threshold and limits of 4 and 8 are test fixtures, not universal recommendations. Calibrate them from labeled questions, then version the policy with the evaluation set. A threshold without a corpus is decoration.

In production, emit one event for each attempt with traceId, stage, collection, limit, resultCount, and a non-sensitive source identifier. Add counters for grounded answers and evidence gaps, plus a distribution for attempts per question. Don't log raw learner questions or chunk text by default; property-management training can contain names, addresses, or policy details that do not belong in broad telemetry access.

Watch the before/after. Before the fallback, you need the Stage 1 hit rate and citation coverage. After it, you need the incremental grounded-answer rate, precision on the newly answered set, and the extra index or query work. One aggregate "RAG success" metric hides the exact decision you are trying to make.

Test cost and retrieval quality together

Build a compact evaluation set before importing the whole PDF folder. Preserve tenant and access-control metadata on every indexed item, then run identical questions through every candidate. Include straightforward lookups, paraphrases, conflicting editions, unauthorized documents, and deliberately unanswerable questions. The expected result for the last group is insufficient_evidence, not a polished guess.

Index cost at scale has two parts: what you store and how often you rebuild it. Track PDF count, parsed page count, chunk count, metadata size, and the number of chunks changed by an update. Then separate one-time ingestion work from recurring query work. No invented savings percentage. Just comparable units from the same corpus and the same access predicates.

A useful release gate is blunt: a backend cannot advance because it is easy to integrate if it violates an access test, and it cannot advance because it retrieves more passages if precision collapses on fallback-only answers. Fast setup is valuable. Correct boundaries are mandatory.

For each candidate, retain the configuration, corpus digest, policy version, and raw result identifiers. That turns a vendor bake-off into a repeatable experiment rather than a meeting driven by screenshots. It also lets the team rerun the test when a new handbook revision doubles one collection or changes the distribution of metadata filters.

Limits and a practical decision

Choose the single managed-index shape when one candidate meets the retrieval and cost gates and the team values low integration overhead. Choose the adapter shape when scale, procurement, or operating policy makes replacement plausible. In both cases, keep the three-stage fallback policy in application code and refuse to broaden tenant or role access.

This design does not choose chunking, embedding, or reranking settings for you. Those require representative PDFs and measured failure cases. It also isn't suitable when the tutor must answer across material a learner is not authorized to read; no retrieval trick turns that into a safe requirement.

Small, explicit, observable. That's the system shape.

If the plain-REST boundary fits your platform, start with the Infrai documentation and inspect the discovery contract before implementing a provider adapter.

References

  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation research paper
  • Pinecone documentation
  • Qdrant documentation
  • Weaviate documentation
  • pgvector repository
  • Infrai documentation

title: Node.js SMS OTP API Login: 3 Retry Boundaries (Template-Owned Verification Code)
description:
Choose a hosted SMS OTP API for US/EU SaaS login, while keeping template ownership, recipient suppression, and abuse admission in the e-commerce application's durable data layer. The deciding constraint is who can change a login message and who can authorize another delivery after a recipient has been suppressed. A successful API request answers neither question.

Short answer: managed code generation, expiry, and verification reduce integration work, but retry policy and rate limiting remain business decisions. For a Node.js storefront, select the provider only after deciding which template revisions and recipient decisions must survive a provider change. Keep those decisions explicit.

Try Infrai for hosted SMS OTP and verification when your team wants the capability contract to stay stable while the vendor behind it changes; pair that boundary with its per-call cost, vendor, and latency metadata to account for retry traffic separately from successful logins. That is a concrete integration and reconciliation benefit. It does not establish equivalent delivery outcomes across vendors, and it does not make the provider the owner of your suppression policy.

Infrai provides a single API key and unified billing through one REST API, with no SDK required. This unified API lets the application switch vendors without changing application code at the capability boundary. Infrai's API is genuinely self-describing, and the discovery surface is public with no key required, so engineers can inspect schemas before wiring the login dispatcher. The trade-off is that transport portability does not transfer ownership of the login policy. Infrai is not a good fit when your requirement is to delegate the entire authentication workflow; evaluate Twilio Verify or Vonage Verify against that requirement instead.

Decision: own the intent, delegate the challenge

This note treats customer login as part of an e-commerce system that also handles email bounces and suppresses invalid recipients. Its three durable boundaries are template intent, recipient eligibility, and challenge authorization. The hosted service manages the SMS challenge; the application decides whether a challenge should be requested at all.

Templates are business data.

Store the approved purpose, locale, revision, and mapping to the selected provider's template identifier in an application-owned registry. A revision such as login-us-en-r3 is an illustrative internal identifier, not a provider field. This gives a reviewer something stable to compare when a supplier changes, although provider-specific content and approval requirements still need review. Contract stability reduces adapter churn; it cannot prove that every template transfers unchanged.

Recipient eligibility needs an equally explicit owner because an email bounce, a failed SMS delivery, and an incorrect verification code describe different events. A permanent invalid-address signal can justify suppressing that email destination under an approved policy. An incorrect code cannot. Nor should an email suppression automatically prohibit an SMS challenge to a separately registered phone number. Treating a customer record as one undifferentiated delivery target creates a particularly expensive failure mode: a marketing-address problem disables account recovery.

The service boundary uses polling for delivery and result tracking. Design the reconciler around that model, with an age limit and a bounded polling budget. For an email fallback, the application owns code generation, expiry, verification, and the decision to send; choose a specialist managed verification service if owning that additional security path is outside the team's scope.

How should a Node.js SaaS login retry an SMS OTP API request?

The invariants are small enough to review without a vendor diagram.

A confirmed suppression prevents future admissions for that channel and destination. Repeating the same admission key does not allocate another send. A changed template revision represents a new decision, rather than silently modifying the meaning of a pending one. A successful verification, rather than a delivery receipt, authorizes login.

Ordering matters.

Delivery isn't authentication.

Consider a bounce reconciler and a login request arriving concurrently. If the request reads eligibility before the reconciler records suppression, some work may already have been admitted when suppression commits; a database transaction can order these decisions, but it cannot recall an external side effect that has already happened. Recheck eligibility before dispatch, keep the dispatch interval short, and document this residual boundary. Do not advertise instantaneous revocation unless the complete dispatch protocol actually provides it.

Retry handling has two layers. A repeated network attempt for the same operation should retain its idempotency key, while a user-requested resend needs a fresh admission decision and its own abuse budget. Infrai specifies an Idempotency-Key convention with a default 24-hour deduplication window; confirm the selected capability's idempotency declaration instead of assuming that every write has identical behavior. Application records may need to outlive that window. Their retention is a policy choice.

A practical rate limiter should account for account, destination, source, and country, with a separate verification-attempt budget. Country eligibility and country spend circuit breakers belong in the application policy. For an HTTP 429, honor Retry-After when present and otherwise use bounded exponential backoff; stop when the login deadline expires. Retrying indefinitely converts a transient limit into a backlog of stale authentication messages.

Compare ownership before comparing transport

The alternatives below are procurement paths, not a measured ranking of delivery performance. Their documentation should be checked against your target countries and actual account configuration before committing to a template or migration plan.

Option Ownership decision Why evaluate it Boundary to test
Infrai hosted SMS OTP Keep application template intent and suppression policy outside the provider contract A stable capability interface reduces vendor-specific integration work; per-call metadata supports workload reconciliation Confirm capability readiness and template mapping; budget for polling and application abuse controls
Twilio Verify Evaluate a dedicated verification product's configuration against your application registry A verification-focused product is a serious alternative when the authentication workflow drives the selection Review supported channel and template controls in its own documentation; do not assume configuration ports to another API
Vonage Verify Decide which verification workflow decisions you delegate to its service Another specialist verification option to include in a US/EU evaluation Test the selected workflow and retry semantics against your suppression and admission invariants
Amazon SNS Retain application ownership of the OTP lifecycle when using messaging primitives A direct messaging approach can fit teams that deliberately own challenge generation and verification Include expiry, replay prevention, and verification-attempt limits in the engineering estimate

Twilio Verify and Vonage Verify deserve evaluation when verification-specific workflow control is the central requirement. Amazon SNS deserves evaluation when messaging transport is the intended boundary and the team accepts the security work above it. None of those choices eliminates the need to decide what an invalid email recipient means for a separate SMS login destination.

Critical path: admit once, suppress by channel

Before wiring the dispatcher, inspect the live capability manifest rather than guessing send or verify fields. This read-only Python example uses the public discovery surface, an explicit method, bounded retries, and an environment-supplied credential. It makes no delivery request, so it needs no write idempotency key. The output is the current manifest for schema review, not evidence that a login succeeded.

import json
import os
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from email.utils import parsedate_to_datetime
from urllib.error import HTTPError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

request = Request(
    "https://api.infrai.cc/v1/discovery",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["INFRAI_API_KEY"]},
    method="GET",
)
deadline = time.monotonic() + 30
for attempt in range(4):
    try:
        with urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
            if response.status != 200:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Unexpected status: {response.status}")
            print(json.dumps(json.load(response), indent=2))
        break
    except HTTPError as error:
        detail = error.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        if error.code != 429 or attempt == 3:
            raise RuntimeError(f"HTTP {error.code}: {detail}") from error
        wait = float(2 ** attempt)
        retry_after = error.headers.get("Retry-After")
        if retry_after:
            try:
                wait = max(wait, float(retry_after))
            except ValueError:
                retry_at = parsedate_to_datetime(retry_after)
                wait = max(wait, (retry_at - datetime.now(timezone.utc)).total_seconds())
        if time.monotonic() + wait >= deadline:
            raise RuntimeError("Retry exceeds discovery deadline") from error
        time.sleep(wait)

The following runnable Python example demonstrates the local consistency boundary, even if the storefront itself uses Node.js. It makes no provider request and uses no invented request fields. SQLite transactions serialize admission and suppression writes within this example; the local admission key is not a substitute for a provider idempotency key. The two must be connected deliberately by a production dispatcher.

import sqlite3

db = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", isolation_level=None)
db.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE suppression (
    channel TEXT NOT NULL,
    destination TEXT NOT NULL,
    reason TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (channel, destination)
);
CREATE TABLE admission (
    operation_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    channel TEXT NOT NULL,
    destination TEXT NOT NULL,
    revision TEXT NOT NULL
);
""")


def suppress(channel, destination, reason):
    db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        db.execute(
            "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO suppression VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (channel, destination, reason),
        )
        db.execute("COMMIT")
    except Exception:
        db.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise


def admit(operation_key, channel, destination, revision):
    db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        prior = db.execute(
            "SELECT channel, destination, revision FROM admission "
            "WHERE operation_key = ?",
            (operation_key,),
        ).fetchone()
        intended = (channel, destination, revision)
        if prior is not None and prior != intended:
            raise ValueError("Admission key reused for different intent")
        blocked = db.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM suppression "
            "WHERE channel = ? AND destination = ?",
            (channel, destination),
        ).fetchone()
        if blocked:
            result = "suppressed"
        elif prior is not None:
            result = "already admitted"
        else:
            db.execute(
                "INSERT INTO admission VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (operation_key, channel, destination, revision),
            )
            result = "admitted"
        db.execute("COMMIT")
        return result
    except Exception:
        db.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise


email = "invalid-recipient@example.com"
phone = "+12025550123"
suppress("email", email, "confirmed invalid destination")
print(admit("email-login-1", "email", email, "login-us-en-r3"))
print(admit("sms-login-1", "sms", phone, "login-us-en-r3"))
print(admit("sms-login-1", "sms", phone, "login-us-en-r3"))

The outputs are suppressed, admitted, and already admitted. The email and phone are synthetic example destinations. No message is sent.

This is intentionally an admission demonstration, not a deployable authentication server. Production needs durable storage, an outbox and dispatcher, authorization for suppression changes, destination normalization, abuse counters, and a verification state machine. A crash after admission but before dispatch must leave recoverable work; a timeout after dispatch must not create an independent send. Those are separate failure modes, and neither is fixed by renaming an admission row to “sent.”

Rejected option: let the delivery provider own eligibility

For this design, reject the shortcut of treating provider delivery status as the master customer eligibility record. It confuses transport evidence with business authorization and makes a supplier change depend on reconstructing historical decisions. Provider suppression facilities can enforce delivery policy, but the application still needs an authoritative record of why a destination became ineligible and which channel that decision affects.

There is a valid narrower use case: a team with one channel, a deliberately provider-owned messaging workflow, and no requirement to carry template decisions across suppliers may accept that coupling. A specialist verification product can also be the better choice when the team wants a managed authentication workflow instead of building email fallback and orchestration around a messaging interface.

For the e-commerce design here, evaluate the full operating bill using an explicitly hypothetical workload: 10,000 initial login challenges, 1,000 independently admitted resends, and at most 2 status checks per admitted challenge. That is 11,000 delivery intents and an upper budget of 22,000 status checks, before verification attempts or email fallback. These figures are planning inputs, not a benchmark, a predicted resend rate, or a claim that polling is billable. Replace them with observed counts after launch.

The accounting boundary should include adapter maintenance, template review, bounce reconciliation, support work for locked-out customers, verification attempts, and any fallback sends. Use per-call metadata to attribute actual service spend, then reconcile it with completed logins and admission records. A low transport charge cannot compensate for an unbounded resend loop; equally, a gateway is valuable only if its stable contract actually removes work from the team's maintained integration surface. For example, a retry admitted under an old template revision should remain attributable to that revision even after a new deployment changes the active template, because otherwise support cannot distinguish a content change from a delivery problem. Preserve that relationship in the application's ledger rather than inferring it later from whichever template happens to be current.

NIST's authenticator guidance also matters: SMS over the public telephone network is a restricted authentication method. A simple integration is not evidence of phishing resistance. Revisit the authentication method itself when the account's risk profile demands stronger assurance.

References

  • Twilio Verify API
  • Vonage Verify documentation
  • Amazon SNS SMS messaging
  • NIST SP 800-63B, authenticator requirements
  • RFC 7489, DMARC, for the email authentication boundary, separate from recipient eligibility.

If this ownership boundary fits your system, start with the capability schemas and conventions in the Infrai documentation index.

〇、一句话结论

这套界面的审美方向是对的（墨与宣、朱砂唯一强调色、纸面无卡片墙），粗糙感不是风格问题，是执行问题：

  • 文档 docs/设计系统.md 已经把规范写到了可执行的程度（对比度实测到小数点、朱砂面积实测到 0.271%、字号为什么固定 84px 都写了原因），
  • 但代码有 12 处以上没跟上这份规范，另有 6 处文档内部自相矛盾；
  • 同时缺 3 件最影响"手感"的东西：拉丁装饰字体没加载、抽屉/列表只能鼠标操作、端上壳的错误提示画成了成功提示。

先改哪三件（30 分钟内可落地，详见 §五）：

四、15 条优化建议（P1 → P3）

每条格式：现状问题 → 具体改法（改前/改后可粘贴）→ 落地说明 → 影响面与风险。
所有选择器、变量名、行号均来自本地源码，可直接检索验证。

建议 1｜端上壳的提示语气被丢掉，且"成功=朱砂红 / 警告=普通灰"与后台正好相反（交互 · 配色）｜P1

  • 现状问题

design/shell.js:24 的 setText 只接受两个参数：

  const setText = (id, v) => { const el = $(id); if (el) el.textContent = v; };

但 design/shell.js:201 / 206 / 209 三处都按三参数调用：

  setText('addrMsg', '浏览器原型改不了地址——要改得在安卓壳里。', 'warn');
  setText('addrMsg', '已保存，正在重新探活…', 'ok');
  setText('addrMsg', ok ? '已连上。' : '连不上，检查地址和端口。', ok ? 'ok' : 'warn');

第三个参数（语气）被静默丢弃；design/shell.html:92 的 <div class="note" id="addrMsg" data-tone="quiet">—</div> 因此永远停在 quiet。结果："已连上"和"连不上"在屏幕上完全一样，都是 .note[data-tone="quiet"] { opacity: .7 } 的浅灰小字。

更严重的是色义在两个文件里是反的：

  /* design/shell.css:274-275 */
  .note[data-tone="ok"]   { color: var(--cinnabar); }  /* 成功 = 红 */
  .note[data-tone="warn"] { color: var(--ink-2); }     /* 警告 = 普通灰 */

而 design/admin.css:670-676 里 warn 才是朱砂。红色在《设计系统.md》§2.1 里的语义是"出问题了"，这里却用来表示"成功"。

  • 具体改法 
   // design/shell.js:24  —— 新增一个带语气的写入函数
   const setText = (id, v) => { const el = $(id); if (el) el.textContent = v; };
  +/** 带语气地写文本：语气写进 data-tone，配色交给 CSS，JS 不碰颜色。 */
  +const setMsg = (id, text, tone = 'quiet') => {
  +  const el = $(id);
  +  if (!el) return;
  +  el.textContent = text;
  +  el.dataset.tone = tone;              // 'ok' | 'warn' | 'quiet'
  +};

   // design/shell.js:201 / 206 / 209
  -setText('addrMsg', '浏览器原型改不了地址——要改得在安卓壳里。', 'warn');
  +setMsg('addrMsg', '浏览器原型改不了地址——要改得在安卓壳里。', 'warn');
  -setText('addrMsg', '已保存，正在重新探活…', 'ok');
  +setMsg('addrMsg', '已保存，正在重新探活…', 'ok');
  -setText('addrMsg', ok ? '已连上。' : '连不上，检查地址和端口。', ok ? 'ok' : 'warn');
  +setMsg('addrMsg', ok ? '已连上。' : '连不上，检查地址和端口。', ok ? 'ok' : 'warn');

   // design/shell.css:274-275 —— 色义与 admin.css 对齐
  -.note[data-tone="ok"] { color: var(--cinnabar); }
  -.note[data-tone="warn"] { color: var(--ink-2); }
  +.note[data-tone="ok"]   { color: var(--ink-2); }
  +.note[data-tone="warn"] { color: var(--cinnabar); }

只靠颜色区分仍然不够（色觉障碍用户读不出"红/灰"），补一个形状符号——这也正好符合《设计系统.md》§八"禁止纯靠颜色表意"的取法：

  +.note[data-tone="ok"]::before   { content: "✓ "; font-family: var(--font-mono); }
  +.note[data-tone="warn"]::before { content: "! "; font-family: var(--font-mono); color: var(--cinnabar); }
  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/shell.js 第 24 行后新增 setMsg，第 201/206/209 行改调用；design/shell.css 第 274–275 行换色并加两条 ::before。
    • 改后效果：点「保存并重连」→ 显示"! 浏览器原型改不了地址——要改得在安卓壳里。"（朱砂 + 感叹号）；探活失败 → "! 连不上，检查地址和端口。"；成功 → "✓ 已连上。"（墨色，不抢朱砂）。
    • 验收方式：浏览器打开 design/shell.html，点「保存并重连」看 #addrMsg 的 data-tone 属性是否变成 warn、文字是否呈朱砂色；用 DevTools 检查 #addrMsg.dataset.tone。
    • 工作量：约 10 分钟（含自测）。
    • 影响面：只有端上壳（shell.html + shell.js + shell.css），不触及后台与客厅屏。
    • 风险：低。注意 design/shell.js:24 的 setText 仍被大量其他调用使用，不要改它的签名，新增函数即可，避免波及 20 余处调用。

建议 2｜后台抽屉没有"浮层"该有的样子：列表行键盘不可达、无遮罩、无 ESC、无焦点回收，小屏直接盖死列表（层级 · 交互）｜P1

  • 现状问题
  1. 列表行只能用鼠标点开。 design/admin.html:129 是 <div class="row" data-i="${i}" aria-selected="false">，design/admin.html:141-146 给它绑 click 打开抽屉。div 不可聚焦、无 tabindex、无 role → 键盘用户按 Tab 走不到列表行，更别说 Enter 打开详情。而且 aria-selected 挂在一个没有 role 的 div 上属于无效 ARIA，屏幕阅读器不会播报选中态。

  2. 抽屉不是模态。 design/admin.css:472 起：

     .drawer {
   position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0;
   width: 420px;
   background: var(--paper-lift);
   border-left: 1px solid var(--rule);
   box-shadow: var(--shadow-panel);
   z-index: 30;
   transform: translateX(100%);
   transition: transform var(--t-base) var(--ease-out);
 }
 .drawer[data-open="1"] { transform: none; }

    没有 role="dialog" / aria-modal / 遮罩 / ESC 关闭 / 焦点回收。打开后焦点仍在列表行上，Tab 会跑到抽屉后面的页面内容里；点抽屉外不关。

  3. 小屏没有兜底。 响应式只写了 @media (max-width: 1100px)，把 .admin__body 改成 176px 侧栏，但 .drawer 仍是 420px 固定宽——1100px 屏上抽屉会盖住整张列表，唯一能操作数据的入口被自己遮住。

  4. 表单焦点环被抹掉。 design/admin.css:838：

     .input:focus, .select:focus { border-color: var(--cinnabar); outline: none; }

    它（0,2,0）压过 design/tokens.css:184-188 的 :where(a,button,input,…) + :focus-visible（:where 部分特异度为 0），于是所有输入框/下拉的 2px 焦点环被 outline: none 干掉，只剩一条边框变色。

  • 具体改法

HTML（design/admin.html）

   <aside class="drawer" id="drawer" data-open="0"
  +       role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="金句详情" aria-hidden="true">

  -    <div class="row" data-i="${i}" aria-selected="false">
  +    <div class="row" data-i="${i}" role="option" aria-selected="false" tabindex="0">

   list.querySelectorAll('.row').forEach(r => {
     r.addEventListener('click', () => { … openDrawer(DATA[+r.dataset.i]); });
  +  r.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
  +    if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') { e.preventDefault(); r.click(); }
  +  });
   });

建议 3｜--font-display 的 Cormorant Garamond 从未加载：后台所有"拉丁装饰大数字"其实都掉回了思源宋体（配色 · 排版）｜P1

  • 现状问题

design/tokens.css:72 定义了：

  --font-display: "Cormorant Garamond", "Noto Serif SC", "Songti SC", serif;

但 design/tokens.css 全文只有 3 条 @font-face（:42 Noto Serif SC 400、:52 Noto Serif SC 700、:59 IBM Plex Mono），没有 Cormorant Garamond 的 @font-face，也没有任何 Google Fonts 链接（grep -rn "fonts.googleapis" design/ → 0 命中）。
→ 第一档永远取不到，浏览器落到第二档 Noto Serif SC。

而 NotoSerifSC-subset.woff2 的字符表 design/fonts/subset_chars.txt 实测含 1940 个字符，包含 0–9 与 A–Z/a–z——所以数字确实有字形，只是没有 Cormorant 的高对比衬线骨架。

受影响的地方（全部是"层级"的承重墙）：

| 选择器 | 位置 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| .stat__n | design/admin.css:212 | 后台 4 个统计大数（52px） |
| .corpus__v | design/admin.css:~250 | 语料池健康度大数（24px） |
| .phead__t | design/admin.css:641 | 每页标题（26px） |
| .daygroup__d | design/admin.css:~900 | 播放记录按天分组标题（19px） |
| 内联 var(--font-display) | design/admin-settings.html:137 | 槽位估算数字（26px） |

同时 font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums（.stat__n、.corpus__v）依赖字体自带的旧式数字；思源宋体子集只有等高数字，这层"书卷气"实际不生效。

一句话：后台看起来"数字和正文一个气质"，不是设计选择，是字体没加载。

  • 具体改法

方案 A（推荐，30 分钟）：把 Cormorant Garamond 的拉丁子集自托管，跟现有流程一致。

  # 与现有 Noto Serif SC 子集同一条流水线，只切 Latin Basic + 常用数字
  pyftsubset /path/to/CormorantGaramond-Regular.ttf \
    --unicodes="U+0020-007E,U+00A0-00FF" \
    --layout-features='kern,liga,onum' \
    --flavor=woff2 \
    --output-file=design/fonts/CormorantGaramond-subset.woff2

   /* design/tokens.css —— 放在 IBM Plex Mono 那条之后 */
  +@font-face {
  +  font-family: "Cormorant Garamond";
  +  src: url("fonts/CormorantGaramond-subset.woff2") format("woff2");
  +  font-weight: 400;
  +  font-style: normal;
  +  font-display: swap;
  +  unicode-range: U+0020-007E, U+00A0-00FF;   /* 只管拉丁，别跟中文抢 */
  +}

   /* design/tokens.css:72 —— 兜底更诚实：加载不到就明确退回宋体，而不是"假装" */
  ---font-display: "Cormorant Garamond", "Noto Serif SC", "Songti SC", serif;
  +--font-display: "Cormorant Garamond", "Noto Serif SC", "Songti SC", serif;

方案 B（0 分钟先止血，10 分钟）：如果暂时不引入新字体文件，就别让装饰位假装是装饰位——把 .stat__n 换成等宽衬线并接受宋体，同时在文档里把"拉丁装饰"这一条标记为未落地：

   /* design/admin.css:212 */
   .stat__n {
  -  font-family: var(--font-display);
  +  font-family: var(--font-display);   /* 方案 A 生效前先落到 Noto Serif SC */
       font-size: 52px;
       line-height: 1;
  +  font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums;  /* 仅当字体支持旧式数字时才有效 */
       color: var(--ink);
       letter-spacing: -.01em;
   }
  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/fonts/ 放 1 个 woff2（≈15–25KB）；design/tokens.css 加 1 条 @font-face。
    • 改后效果：.stat__n 的 52px 数字变成高对比细衬线（拉丁装饰体），后台"大数字 / 小标签"这一层立刻从宋体里跳出来——这是《设计系统.md》§七"统计数字用 Cormorant Garamond 48px，oldstyle-nums"本来的样子。
    • 验收方式：Chrome DevTools → Elements → 点 .stat__n → Computed → font-family 第一档应为 Cormorant Garamond，Rendered Fonts 面板应显示该字体命中；数字 0/1/2 应呈现带下沉部的旧式数字（1 有小衬线、7 不带横杠）。
    • 工作量：30 分钟（下载字体 + 子集化 + 校验体积 + 接入）。
    • 影响面：全局令牌，但只影响使用 --font-display 的 5 处。注意：因为 unicode-range 只覆盖拉丁，中文字符仍走 Noto Serif SC，不会出现"中文变拉丁字体缺字"。
    • 风险：低-中。唯一要注意的是子集字符表要同步更新——design/fonts/subset_chars.txt 现在含 A–Z/a–z/0–9（实测确认），拉丁显示字体不必切中文；但若日后有英文专名/年份超出 ASCII，需要把对应码位加进 --unicodes。

建议 4｜字号刻度与《设计系统.md》对不上，而且没有落成令牌（排版）｜P2

  • 现状问题

文档 §三/§七给了明确的字号刻度，代码却各写各的：

| 文档要求 | 代码现状 | 位置 |
|---|---|---|
| 统计数字 48px | font-size: 52px | design/admin.css:212 .stat__n |
| 后台标题 28px / 600 / 行高 1.4 | font-size: 26px; line-height: 1; font-weight: 400; font-family: var(--font-display) —— 四项全不符 | design/admin.css:641 .phead__t |
| 元信息 12px / 行高 1.5 | font-size: 12.5px，没有 line-height → 继承 .admin 的 1.75 | design/admin.css:221 .stat__l |
| 元信息 12px（等宽） | font-size: 10.5px（表头 .tbl th、分组标签 .sec__label、表单标签 .field__l） | design/admin.css:~690 / ~840 / ~860 |
| 元信息 12px | font-size: 9.5px —— 全站最小字 | design/admin.css:979 .bars__ax span |

文档 §三明确写过"字号另有一套，不受 8px 约束"，也就是说字号本该有刻度，但刻度只活在 Markdown 里，代码里没有对应令牌，于是每个组件各写各的。

另外 .phead__t 用 var(--font-display) 显示中文标题（"播放计划""设备"）——Cormorant Garamond 没有中文字形，中文必然回落到 Noto Serif SC 子集，于是标题在"装饰体 → 宋体"之间断了一次，字体栈语义也不干净。

建议 5｜朱砂被当成"通用强调色"用了 45 处，超出"只允许出现在四个地方"的约束（配色 · 层级）｜P2

  • 现状问题

《设计系统.md》§2.1 写死了：朱砂是印泥的颜色，只允许出现在四个地方（印章、序号、进度线、后台"接受入库"主按钮与高分标记），且面积 ≤ 5%。

代码现状：

  • design/admin.css：32 处 var(--cinnabar)；design/shell.css：13 处；
  • design/tokens.css:186 连焦点环也是朱砂。

超出四处的典型：当前侧栏项左边条（admin.css:~129）、选中页签下划线（:~330）、选中行左侧 inset 条（:~404）、.badge--on、.sw[aria-checked="true"]、.input:focus 边框、.note[data-tone="warn"]、.err、.wrow__del:hover、.savebar__msg[warn]、.corpus[data-state="low"]、.btn--primary 及其 hover。

§13.3 实测朱砂面积在客厅屏只有 0.271%（余量 18 倍），但那是客厅屏的数字。后台页一屏里：当前侧栏项 + 选中页签 + 选中行 + 一条 warn 说明 + 焦点环 + 一个朱砂按钮，朱砂面积早已越过 5%，而且开始承担不该承担的功能——"这一行被选中了"和"这里出错了"用同一种红，语义被冲淡。

另外 §七"主按钮只有两个"也没有守住：朱砂实心按钮共 6 个（admin.html:80 立即抓取、:92 接受入库、admin-settings.html:38/:156、admin-sources.html:127、admin-devices.html:119）。§九 减法清单第 7 条"一屏上有几个按钮？超过 2 个 → 合并或降级为文字动作"也没过。

    没有任何 :hover，.sbtn--primary 也没有。两个页面的主按钮手感不一致：后台有 hover 变色，端上只有按下缩放。

建议 7｜.note 在两个文件里同名两义，data-tone 契约是断的（层级 · 配色）｜P2

  • 现状问题

同名组件、两套语义：

  /* design/shell.css:267-276 —— 端上壳：一条灰字说明 */
  .note { padding: 10px 0 2px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--ink-3); }
  .note[data-tone="ok"] { color: var(--cinnabar); }   /* 成功 = 红 */
  .note[data-tone="warn"] { color: var(--ink-2); }    /* 警告 = 灰 */
  .note[data-tone="quiet"] { opacity: .7; }

  /* design/admin.css:660-680 —— 后台：一张带左边线的说明条 */
  .note {
    margin: 0 0 var(--s-3);
    padding: var(--s-2) var(--s-2) var(--s-2) var(--s-3);
    border-left: 2px solid var(--rule-strong);
    background: var(--paper-lift);
    font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.7;
    color: var(--ink-2); letter-spacing: .02em;
  }
  .note[data-tone="warn"] { border-left-color: var(--cinnabar); color: var(--ink); background: var(--cinnabar-soft); }
  .note[data-tone="quiet"] { background: none; color: var(--ink-3); font-size: 12.5px; }

差异有四层：形状（灰字 vs 带边线的卡片）、字号（12 vs 13）、语义映射（ok/warn 颜色相反）、宽度（端上是窄屏通栏、后台是内容栏）。同一个 data-tone="warn" 在两个页面表达两件事。

根因是 §7.1 表格里把 .note 列为"从 shell.css 搬过来"的共用件，但代码里是复制，不是共用——两份定义各写各的。

  • 具体改法

第一步：定义一份契约（写进 docs/设计系统.md §7.1 的表格里）：

| data-tone | 语义 | 颜色 | 形状标记 |
|---|---|---|---|
| quiet | 补充信息，不重要 | --ink-3 | 无 |
| ok | 成功/已完成 | --ink-2 | ✓ 前缀 |
| warn | 出错了/需要你管 | --cinnabar | ! 前缀 |

第二步：把"共用件"真的抽成共用。design/shell.css 删掉自己的 .note 定义，改为引用 admin.css 的形状 + 一个窄屏字号变体：

   /* design/shell.css —— 删掉 :267-276 整段 .note 定义 */
  -.note { padding: 10px 0 2px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--ink-3); }
  -.note[data-tone="ok"] { color: var(--cinnabar); }
  -.note[data-tone="warn"] { color: var(--ink-2); }
  -.note[data-tone="quiet"] { opacity: .7; }

端上壳改为在 design/shell.html:7-8 多引一个 admin.css？——不推荐（会把后台的 1106 行整个带进壳页）。更好的做法是新建 design/note.css（共用件单文件），两个页面都引：

  /* design/note.css（新增，共用件） */
  .note {
    margin: 0 0 var(--s-3);
    padding: var(--s-2) var(--s-2) var(--s-2) var(--s-3);
    border-left: 2px solid var(--rule-strong);
    background: var(--paper-lift);
    font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.7;
    color: var(--ink-2); letter-spacing: .02em;
  }
  .note[data-tone="warn"]  { border-left-color: var(--cinnabar); color: var(--ink); background: var(--cinnabar-soft); }
  .note[data-tone="quiet"] { background: none; color: var(--ink-3); font-size: 12.5px; }
  .note[data-tone="ok"]    { background: none; color: var(--ink-2); }
  .note[data-tone="ok"]::before   { content: "✓ "; font-family: var(--font-mono); }
  .note[data-tone="warn"]::before { content: "! "; font-family: var(--font-mono); color: var(--cinnabar); }

  /* 窄屏变体：端上壳用 */
  .note--sm { margin: 0; padding: 10px 0 2px; border-left: 0; background: none; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.6; }

   /* design/shell.html:7-9 */
     <link rel="stylesheet" href="tokens.css">
  +<link rel="stylesheet" href="note.css">
     <link rel="stylesheet" href="shell.css">

   /* design/shell.html —— 两处 .note 换成窄屏变体 */
  -<div class="note" id="addrMsg" data-tone="quiet">—</div>
  +<div class="note note--sm" id="addrMsg" data-tone="quiet">—</div>

   /* design/admin.css —— 删掉重复的 .note 段，改为引入共用件 */
  -.note { … }          /* 删掉 admin.css:660-680 这一段 */
  +/* .note 见 design/note.css（与端上壳共用） */

   /* design/admin.html:7-9 与其余 5 个后台页 */
     <link rel="stylesheet" href="tokens.css">
  +<link rel="stylesheet" href="note.css">
     <link rel="stylesheet" href="admin.css">
  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：新增 design/note.css；design/admin.css 删 1 段；design/shell.css 删 1 段；design/shell.html + 6 个后台页各加 1 行 <link>、1 处 class 加 note--sm。
    • 改后效果：同一条说明在后台与端上壳形状一致、语义一致，只有字号随栏宽变化；data-tone 有了可查的契约，不会再出现"这个颜色在这个页面是成功、在那个页面是错误"。
    • 验收方式：① 端上壳点「保存并重连」看 warn 样式（朱砂左边线 + "!" 前缀）；② 后台"播放计划"页的约束违规说明条形状相同；③ grep -rn "\.note" design/*.css 只在 note.css 命中。
    • 工作量：30 分钟（新建 1 个文件 + 8 处引用改动）。
    • 影响面：后台 7 页 + 端上壳；客厅屏不引用 .note。
    • 风险：中低。注意加载顺序：note.css 必须在 admin.css/shell.css 之前，否则后者的规则会覆盖共用件（.note 同特异度时后者胜）。如果嫌多一个文件，退一步的做法是只统一语义映射、不动形状：把 shell.css 的 ok/warn 颜色对调，10 分钟搞定，契约先立起来。

建议 8｜端上壳底栏的「播放」「日志」两个 Tab 是死按钮（交互）｜P2

  • 现状问题 
  <!-- design/shell.html:130-132 -->
  <nav class="tabbar">
    <button aria-current="page">设备</button>
    <button>播放</button>
    <button>日志</button>
  </nav>

  /* design/shell.js —— 底栏处理器 */
  document.querySelectorAll('.tabbar button').forEach(b => {
    b.addEventListener('click', () => {
      document.querySelectorAll('.tabbar button').forEach(x => x.removeAttribute('aria-current'));
      b.setAttribute('aria-current', 'page');
    });
  });

点击后只移动高亮条，页面内容一点不变。 「播放」「日志」是典型的"看起来是功能但其实没用的元素"，直接违反 §八 与 §九 减法清单第 5/10 条（§13.2 记录的"删：客厅屏在线指示器"就是同一类问题的正确处理方式）。

这也是整个界面"看着粗糙"的一个来源：底栏给了用户三个位置的心智预期，但只有一个是真的。

  • 具体改法

方案 A（推荐，20 分钟）：删掉假 Tab，只留真实内容。

   <!-- design/shell.html:130-132 -->
    <nav class="tabbar">
  -  <button aria-current="page">设备</button>
  -  <button>播放</button>
  -  <button>日志</button>
  +  <button aria-current="page">设备</button>
    </nav>

   /* design/shell.css —— 单项底栏改成左对齐的标题条 */
   .tabbar {
     position: fixed;
     left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0;
     height: 64px;
  -  display: grid;
  -  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
  +  display: flex;
  +  align-items: center;
  +  justify-content: center;
     background: var(--paper-lift);
     border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
     z-index: 20;
   }

方案 B（60 分钟）：真的做成三个页签。 把 shell.html 的内容拆成三段，用 hidden 属性切换：

  -<section class="sec">…设备…</section>
  +<section class="sec" data-pane="device">…设备…</section>
  +<section class="sec" data-pane="play" hidden>…播放时段与音量…</section>
  +<section class="sec" data-pane="log" hidden>…日志…</section>

  /* design/shell.js —— 真的切换内容 */
  document.querySelectorAll('.tabbar button').forEach(b => {
    b.addEventListener('click', () => {
      document.querySelectorAll('.tabbar button').forEach(x => x.removeAttribute('aria-current'));
      b.setAttribute('aria-current', 'page');
      const pane = b.dataset.pane;
      document.querySelectorAll('[data-pane]').forEach(p => {
        p.hidden = p.dataset.pane !== pane;      // 真的换内容
      });
      window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'instant' });
    });
  });

若选方案 B，"日志"页要有真实内容才成——shell.js 现在没有日志来源，需要原生桥提供；没有内容就只做方案 A。

  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/shell.html:130-132、design/shell.css 的 .tabbar、design/shell.js 底栏处理器。
    • 改后效果：底栏要么诚实（只有一个真页签），要么真的能切（三屏内容切换）。不再有"点了没反应"的按钮。
    • 验收方式：点底栏每一项，页面内容必须有可见变化或该项不存在；用 grep -c "<button" design/shell.html 确认假 Tab 已移除。
    • 工作量：方案 A 20 分钟；方案 B 60 分钟 + 需要原生日志接口。
    • 影响面：仅端上壳。.shell { padding-bottom: 96px }（design/shell.css:16）是为 64px 底栏留的，改底栏宽度不影响它，但方案 B 若底栏变高要同步调 padding。
    • 风险：低。方案 A 会被"底栏太空"质疑——若真觉得空，把 .tabbar 改成一行居中的说明（"长按屏幕可回到客厅屏"已经在 .sec--last 里出现过，正好上移到底栏，一次只说一次）。

建议 9｜客厅屏金句的 CSS 兜底字号是 6.25vw（＝120px），与"固定 84px"冲突，首帧会跳字（排版）｜P3

  • 现状问题 
  /* design/board.css:99 */
  .quote__text {
    margin: 0;
    font-weight: 400;
    font-size: var(--q-size, 6.25vw);
    line-height: 1.55;
    letter-spacing: .04em;
    color: var(--ink);
    text-wrap: balance;
  }

--q-size 由 design/board.js 的 fitQuote() 写入（Q_SIZE = 84），但那是 JS 执行之后。在 JS 还没跑的那一帧（WebView 冷启动、脚本被缓存策略推迟、JS 报错），兜底值 6.25vw 在 1920 屏上 = 120px，比终态 84px 大 43%。

《设计系统.md》§三 写得很明确："金句字号：固定 84px"；§13.4 又用实测数据论证了 84px 的合理性。既然结论是"固定"，兜底值就不该是另一个数——这是规范与代码的直接冲突，也是"一眼看上去字在跳"的唯一来源。

  • 具体改法 
   /* design/board.css:99 */
   .quote__text {
     margin: 0;
     font-weight: 400;
  -  font-size: var(--q-size, 6.25vw);
  +  font-size: var(--q-size, 84px);   /* 兜底就等于规范值；首帧即终态 */
     line-height: 1.55;
     letter-spacing: .04em;
     color: var(--ink);
     text-wrap: balance;
   }

（若要让它随屏幕等比缩放，把 84px 写成 min(84px, 4.375vw)——4.375vw × 1920 = 84px，小屏同步缩小，且永远不超过规范值。这比 6.25vw 更符合"客厅屏等比适配"的意图。）

  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/board.css:99，1 行。
    • 改后效果：客厅屏第一帧就是 84px，不再出现"先大后小"的跳变；顺带解决了低分辨率盒子上的字号溢出。
    • 验收方式：Chrome 打开 design/board.html?theme=dawn&mode=play，用 DevTools 把 JS 禁用后再看，金句字号应仍是 84px 而不是 120px；1920 屏上量测 getBoundingClientRect().height / 行数。
    • 工作量：1 分钟。
    • 影响面：只有客厅屏；fitQuote() 写入 --q-size 后行为不变（内联变量优先级高于兜底值）。
    • 风险：无。这是全方案里性价比最高的一条。

建议 10｜文档 §2.2 定义的 --sheen 令牌在代码里根本不存在（配色）｜P3

  • 现状问题

《设计系统.md》§2.2 明写："唯一允许的"渐变"是背景的 --sheen（径向），模拟一束灯光从上方 26% 处打在纸上；除此之外全站禁止渐变。"

实测：grep -rn "sheen" design/ → 0 命中。晨/夜两层径向渐变是硬编码在 design/board.css:24-25：

  .board__bg--dawn  { background: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 26%, #F8F3E9 0%, #F1EBDD 52%, #E6DECC 100%); }
  .board__bg--night { background: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 22%, #15130F 0%, #0D0C0A 55%, #060605 100%); opacity: 0; }

后果：令牌表少了一个语义层。想调灯光角度/亮度必须去改 board.css 的字面量，而不是改令牌；后台页与端上壳没有灯光层，"唯一允许的渐变"实际只有客厅屏一处硬编码——规范没被执行，只是碰巧一致。

  • 具体改法 
   /* design/tokens.css —— 晨主题 */
   .theme-dawn {
     …
  +  /* 灯光层：径向，从上方 26% 处打在纸上（§2.2 唯一允许的渐变） */
  +  --sheen: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 26%, #F8F3E9 0%, #F1EBDD 52%, #E6DECC 100%);
   }

   /* design/tokens.css —— 夜主题 */
   .theme-night {
     …
  +  --sheen: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 22%, #15130F 0%, #0D0C0A 55%, #060605 100%);
   }

   /* design/board.css:24-25 —— 改成引用令牌 */
   -.board__bg--dawn  { background: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 26%, #F8F3E9 0%, #F1EBDD 52%, #E6DECC 100%); }
   -.board__bg--night { background: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 22%, #15130F 0%, #0D0C0A 55%, #060605 100%); opacity: 0; }
  +.board__bg--dawn  { background: var(--sheen); }
  +.board__bg--night { background: var(--sheen); opacity: 0; }

注意：两层背景仍必须分开保留（board.css:18-21 的注释解释了原因——渐变不可插值，主题切换靠两层交叉淡 opacity）。只把渐变值抽成令牌，不要把两层合并成一层。

  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/tokens.css 两个主题各加 1 行，design/board.css 2 行改写。
    • 改后效果：灯光层从"代码里的魔法值"变成"令牌表里的一格"；§2.2 的规范第一次真的被执行到代码里。
    • 验收方式：切 theme-dawn / theme-night，客厅屏灯光过渡仍然是 1200ms 交叉淡入（不能变成硬切）；grep -c "radial-gradient" design/board.css → 0。
    • 工作量：20 分钟。
    • 影响面：客厅屏背景层；渐变值本身不变，视觉零差异（纯结构收益）。
    • 风险：低。唯一要确认的是自定义属性里放 radial-gradient 在目标 WebView 版本上可用（Android 5+ 的 WebView 全部支持 CSS 自定义属性，值类型不限）。

建议 13｜aria-selected 挂在没有 role 的 div 上；页签缺 tabpanel 与方向键（层级 · 交互）｜P3

  • 现状问题
  1. design/admin.html:129：<div class="row" data-i="${i}" aria-selected="false"> —— aria-selected 只对 option/row/tab/gridcell 等有隐含或显式 role 的元素有意义。放在裸 div 上属于无效 ARIA，屏幕阅读器不播报，用户也无法知道哪一条被选中。
  2. design/admin.html:77：<div class="tabs" role="tablist"> + <button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="…">，但没有 role="tabpanel"、没有 aria-controls、没有 id 配对；design/admin-play.html:43 的时间范围页签同样。页签容器 role="tablist" 里也没有 aria-label。
  3. 所有页签都留在 Tab 序列里（没有 roving tabindex），键盘用户要在页签间按 3 次 Tab 才能到内容。
  • 具体改法 
   /* design/admin.html —— 列表用 listbox/option 语义 */
  -<div class="list" id="list"></div>
  +<div class="list" id="list" role="listbox" aria-label="候选金句"></div>

  -    <div class="row" data-i="${i}" aria-selected="false">
  +    <div class="row" data-i="${i}" role="option" aria-selected="false" tabindex="0">

   /* design/admin.html —— 页签补齐 tablist/tab/tabpanel 三件套 */
  -<div class="tabs" role="tablist">
  -  ${TABS.map((t) => `<button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="${t.status === CURRENT}" data-status="${t.status}">${t.label}<span class="tab__n" id="tab-${t.status}">0</span></button>`).join('')}
  -</div>
  +<div class="tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="金句状态">
  +  ${TABS.map((t, i) => `<button class="tab" role="tab" id="tabbtn-${t.status}" aria-controls="tabpanel" aria-selected="${t.status === CURRENT}" tabindex="${i === 0 ? 0 : -1}" data-status="${t.status}">${t.label}<span class="tab__n" id="tab-${t.status}">0</span></button>`).join('')}
  +</div>

  -<div class="list" id="list" role="listbox" aria-label="候选金句"></div>
  +<div class="list" id="list" role="listbox" aria-label="候选金句" id="tabpanel" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="tabbtn-${CURRENT}" tabindex="0"></div>

同一个元素不能同时有两个 id；落地时把 role="tabpanel" 单独挂在 .list 上，aria-labelledby 用当前页签按钮的 id 动态更新。

方向键（页签漫游）：

  /* design/admin.html —— 页签支持左右方向键 */
  const tabBtns = [...document.querySelectorAll('.tabs .tab')];
  tabBtns.forEach((t, i) => {
    t.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
      const dir = e.key === 'ArrowRight' ? 1 : e.key === 'ArrowLeft' ? -1 : 0;
      if (!dir) return;
      e.preventDefault();
      const next = tabBtns[(i + dir + tabBtns.length) % tabBtns.length];
      next.focus();
      next.click();
    });
  });
  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/admin.html（.list 容器、.row 模板、.tabs 模板、页签事件）、design/admin-play.html:43（时间范围页签同样补 aria-label）。
    • 改后效果：屏幕阅读器能播报"列表框 / 3 个选项 / 第 1 个已选中"；页签可用左右方向键切换，Tab 序列缩短。
    • 验收方式：用 macOS VoiceOver（Cmd+F5）或 Chrome DevTools 的 Elements → Accessibility 面板，确认选中项被播报；键盘按 ←/→ 能切页签。
    • 工作量：30 分钟。
    • 影响面：后台列表与页签；纯语义层，不影响任何视觉。
    • 风险：低-中。role="option" 的元素必须在 role="listbox" 内，且列表项要可聚焦（tabindex="0"）；若一次只让当前项可聚焦（roving tabindex）更好，但要处理 render() 重绘后的焦点复位——第一版可以先不做。

建议 14｜正文用粗体做强调：既违反 §八，又和 §7.2 自相矛盾（排版）｜P3

  • 现状问题

《设计系统.md》里有两条互相打架的规则：

  • §八 禁止清单："禁止在正文里用粗体做强调（中文粗体显廉价，改用字号或颜色差）"
  • §7.2 第 3 条："说明条里的重点用 <strong>，不用朱砂 —— 朱砂留给「出问题了」，不是「这里是重点」"

代码选了"粗体"那条：

  /* design/admin.css:684 */
  .note strong {
    font-weight: 600;
    color: var(--ink);
  }
  .note[data-tone="warn"] strong { color: var(--cinnabar-ink); }

而 design/admin.js 的 emphasis() 还会把 **这样** 转成 <strong>——每次调用 note() 都在制造粗体。

这是全项目唯一一处规范本身没定清楚的地方，也是发布者最可能忽略、但一眼能看出的"AI 味"来源。

  • 具体改法

改代码：用"着重"代替"加粗"，同时满足两条规则。

   .note strong {
  -  font-weight: 600;
  -  color: var(--ink);
  +  font-weight: 400;                        /* 不加粗 */
  +  color: var(--ink);                        /* 用墨色差表达重点 */
  +  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);   /* 着重线 */
  +  padding-bottom: 1px;
   }
   .note[data-tone="warn"] strong {
     color: var(--cinnabar-ink);
  +  border-bottom-color: currentColor;
   }

改文档：把 §七/§八 的矛盾显式解掉。

   - - 禁止在正文里用粗体做强调（中文粗体显廉价，改用字号或颜色差）
  + - 禁止在正文里用粗体做强调（中文粗体显廉价，改用**字号、墨色深浅或着重线**）
  +   （唯一例外：§7.2 的说明条重点用「着重线 + 墨色」表达，同样不用粗体）

   §7.2 第 3 条
  - 3. **说明条里的重点用 `<strong>`，不用朱砂**。
  + 3. **说明条里的重点用 `<strong>` + 着重线，不用朱砂、不用粗体**。

若你更看重"一眼可见"，另一种合法解法是用字号差（与 §八 原话一致）：

   .note strong { font-weight: 400; font-size: 1.06em; color: var(--ink); }

但字号差会让说明条行高跳动，推荐着重线方案。

  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/admin.css:684-690、docs/设计系统.md §八 禁止清单与 §7.2 第 3 条。
    • 改后效果：说明条里的重点由"粗体"变成"墨色 + 下划细线"，与整页的宋体气质一致；《设计系统.md》也不再自相矛盾。

    • 影响面：后台 7 页的说明条；design/admin.js 的 emphasis() 不用改（它只负责生成 <strong>，样式在 CSS）。
    • 风险：低。

  +     2. 朱砂选中条 `2px`
  +     3. 图表刻度间隙 `3px`（§7.1 迷你柱状、评分格）
